title: Roguelike Slaying: Enemy Density Formulas and Screen Readability
subtitle: This article dissects the core mechanics of roguelike slaying games, breaking down the construction of enemy density curves to create dynamic combat pacing. It explains how director systems use calculation to control enemy distribution for screen readability, analyzes hard rules limiting special effects to ensure visual clarity, and reveals the satisfaction derived from linear enemy growth paired with exponential player damage. The guide provides actionable advice for developers to balance numerical values with player experience.

breakdown.title: Enemy Density Curve
bullets: Use a 'spawn budget per unit time' instead of fixed refresh intervals
Curve segmentation recommendation: fast start for gratification → stable middle section → explosive late game
Density = Quantity × Speed × Size; all three cannot be maximized simultaneously

breakdown.title: Screen Readability (Hard Rules)
bullets: Bullet/Special Effect Cap: downsample or merge visuals if exceeded
Player Silhouette Must Be Clear: high-contrast outlines and center-screen negative space
Priority for Hazard Information: damage zones, projectiles, and enemy dashes must be most prominent

breakdown.title: Satisfaction Sources
bullets: Stepwise escalation in clear efficiency: noticeable power-ups every 1~2 minutes
'On the Brink of Death' Window: buffer frames for player reaction
Map numerical growth to visuals: larger range, longer chains, and stronger knockbacks
